subject: ADR-155: the instrument in the measurement -- the harness fill counter was a shared global
body: THE INSTRUMENT WAS IN THE MEASUREMENT. Setting out to close the twelve accepted layout spills on selection-log and survey-design carried since ADR-103, none could be reproduced by opening the page. tools/harness.py keeps a fill counter -- every field-fill a different value, so a field filled with what it already holds is not mistaken for one wired to nothing -- and it was a MODULE GLOBAL SHARED BY EVERY PAGE IN THE RUN. survey-design driven ALONE is filled with harness-3; driven as page 35 of 41 it is harness-378, three characters wider, and a row that fitted 390 px stops fitting. The same two pages, unedited, sit in this repo's own ledgers at three answers (38/0 pre-ADR-128, 38/23 on 08-31, 0/0 today); ADR-128 had ALREADY fixed the one real defect on 09-02 but the baseline never noticed, because the number it was meant to move had stopped being a property of the page. And WHETHER THE KIT WAS GREEN DEPENDED ON WALK ORDER, which under -j2 is thread scheduling -- flaky, not merely order-dependent: invariant breaks read 0, 38 or 61 depending on the run. THE FIX is threading.local() reset at the top of each page, thread-local rather than merely reset per page because the run drives two pages at once and a plain global assignment would leave the two walks clobbering each other. THE SPILL REPORT ALSO POINTED NOWHERE -- the first two matches in document order are the outermost containers, innocent by construction, printed with a width alone (w=372 looks fine until you know the box starts at x=33); it now names the outermost element WHOSE PARENT STILL FITS with its span and overrun (div.row2 x=33..427, +37 past 390) and the value typed. verify_harness_matrix gains SECTION L, six checks (71 -> 77): a page measured after another measures the same; the fixture really driven both times; the counter restarts at one per page; two walks at once do not share it; the accounting holds; and L6, no module-level state in harness.py written during a run, an AST rule so the NEXT cross-page counter is caught before it invents a defect. SECTION F CLAIMED DETERMINISM SINCE ADR-109 AND PASSED EVERY RUN because it compares bucket counts on a fixture WITH NO TEXT INPUT, so the counter never advanced: A PROMISE CHECKED ONLY WHERE IT CANNOT BE BROKEN IS NOT CHECKED. Two of the three new mutants survived the first version of the new checks -- L1 was a comparison inheriting the pollution, L4's two threads never overlapped -- and were repaired by asserting an ABSOLUTE fact (first fill is harness-1) and a threading.Barrier that makes the walks actually contend. mutate_harness 15 -> 18 (18 killed), verify_harness_matrix 71 -> 77, verify_findings RED -> 12/12, accepted debt 13 distinct -> 1 (stand-sheet's one dead control), NO PAGE EDITED and no coverage moved. THE NAME: the instrument was not mistaken about the page, the instrument was IN the measurement -- its own accumulated state changed what it found while every layer above balanced faithfully -- and the defence is that ANY STATE A TOOL CARRIES ACROSS THE THINGS IT MEASURES MUST BE RESET BETWEEN THEM, AND SOMETHING HAS TO ASSERT THAT IT WAS. Delivered as its own commit: this slice authored by a parallel session; its shared bookkeeping (board, counts, AI_HARNESS) lands in the ADR-156 commit that follows, which regenerates them with both slices present.
